subject: How to generate population covariance matrix using lavaan?

messages.author: 84f884ae54fe0da9
messages.subject: How to generate population covariance matrix using lavaan?
parts:
Hi,
 
I tried to generate population covariance matrix using lavaan by using the following codes:
model <- '
  x1 ~ .3*x2  + .4*x3
  x4 ~ .6*x1 + .1*x2 + .2*x3
  x2 ~ .3*x3
'
lav <- lavaanify(model, fixed.x = FALSE)
cov <- fitted(sem(lav))$cov
 
However, the diagonal of matrix I generated are not equal to 1.
Do you have any ideas to generate the population covariance matrix having the diagonal equal to 1?
Thanks a lot!!!
 
Best Regards,
Iris Sun

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: How to generate population covariance matrix using lavaan?
parts:
On 01/06/2015 08:54 AM, Rongwei Sun wrote:
> Hi,
> I tried to generate population covariance matrix using lavaan by using
> the following codes:
> model <- '
> x1 ~ .3*x2 + .4*x3
> x4 ~ .6*x1 + .1*x2 + .2*x3
> x2 ~ .3*x3
> '
> lav <- lavaanify(model, fixed.x = FALSE)

Wow, you are driving without a seatbelt! Since you do not say anything
about the (residual) variances, they will be set to zero.

Either specify all the variances (for x1,x2,x3 and x4) explicitly in
your model syntax, or use

lav <- lavaanify(model, fixed.x = FALSE, auto = TRUE)

and they will be set to 1.
> However, the diagonal of matrix I generated are not equal to 1.
Of course not. Why would they be 1?

> Do you have any ideas to generate the population covariance matrix
> having the diagonal equal to 1?

You will have to adjust the (residual) variances... Look at the formula
of how the model-implied covariance matrix is computed, and you should
be able to figure it out.

Yves.
